title: WeaveCube: A Feasibility Study of Exact Shared-Word Construction for Rubik's Cube Solving
abstract: We study the feasibility of exact shared-word construction in WeaveCube, a Rubik's Cube research system developed within the two-phase solver lineage. The project calls this organization the Lee Weave Method: conditions retain a common move-word identity, exact necessary restrictions reduce a candidate relation, and explicit combinations or complete witness families are formed only when needed. We formalize the scope required for sound restriction and distinguish verified witnesses from exhaustive negative results. In a planted-positive 5+5 mechanism experiment, two banks of 577,368 words define 333,353,807,424 conceptual index pairs; joint signatures restrict this relation before small candidate sets are materialized. Two ordering policies, evaluated in an adaptive-fixed-adaptive sequence on the same eight cases, each found replay-verified witnesses; median condition counts were 8, 10, and 8. A separate historical local-closure experiment reports 15.4988 s for a vectorized first-witness configuration versus 36.8624 s for the geometric mean of two full-closure controls, while a later total-economics experiment did not show a lower total wall after preparation overhead. Neither result establishes a general speedup. Separately, a frozen operational driver historically returned replay-checked solutions for 24 deterministic, hash-derived, 25-move scrambles. A new reproduction run using the same sealed corpus and frozen D6 asset serialized all 24 complete solution words and replayed each again natively; an independent fixed-frame 54-sticker implementation with no CubeLab/WeaveCube import also replayed all 24 scramble-solution pairs to the solved state. Historical timings remain attached only to the original run. These results should be read primarily as a feasibility demonstration: the proposed shared-word construction can be implemented and can produce valid solutions in the tested settings. They do not establish reliable coverage of arbitrary cube states, consistently short solutions, computational scalability, or competitive performance relative to mature solvers. The architecture nevertheless exposes concrete questions about coverage, scaling, construction policy, and solution quality for future study.

title: Dahal Jeet: game engine, agents and experimental record
abstract: First public release, accompanying the manuscript "Search-based agents outperform reinforcement learning in Dahal Jeet, a Nepali imperfect-information card game", under review at Scientific Reports. Contains the game engine, 26 agents spanning hand-written heuristics, metaheuristic tuning, PIMC and single- and multiple-observer ISMCTS, and seven families of learning agent; every trained checkpoint; the complete result artifacts behind the paper; and the compute record. Every reported value is generated from an artifact rather than typed: paper_numbers.py emits them as LaTeX macros, paper_tables.py builds the tables, and verify_equations.py recomputes 30 of the manuscript's identities directly against the stored artifacts without re-running any experiment. All 30 pass. Code is MIT; data, models and figures are CC BY 4.0.

title: Identification of granitic pegmatites based on GF-5 hyperspectral data and LSTM-Transformer model
abstract: Lithium is a key strategic mineral to support new energy and advanced technology, mainly enriched in granitic pegmatite. The integration of hyperspectral remote sensing and deep learning frameworks has emerged as a leading approach for quantitative identification of pegmatites. However, deep learning algorithms are often limited by the scarcity of labeled samples and the challenge of extracting features from high-dimensional spectral data. In this study, a data augmentation-driven LSTM-Transformer framework is proposed for pegmatite mapping using GF-5 hyperspectral remote sensing data. In view of limited samples, this study constructed an enhanced training data set by integrating field-measured and infrared scanning spectra, simulating real spectral variability and linear mixing to improve data diversity. The proposed LSTM-Transformer architecture combines LSTM’s advantages in local sequence feature modeling and Transformer’s capacity to capture long-range global relationships, thereby enhancing the detection of weakly diagnostic spectral features. The framework was demonstrated in the Jingerquan lithium deposit, Xinjiang, China. The high-probability areas delineated by the proposed model successfully captured several pegmatite dikes documented in previous geological studies. The prediction results were further validated through field sampling. Geochemical analyses of specimens collected from the predicted high-probability target areas show an average Li 2 O grade of 7.86 wt.%, which meets industrial requirements and confirms the reliability of the proposed method. Overall, these results provide the potential of the proposed framework for pegmatite mapping and subsequent mineral exploration under the conditions of limited labeled samples.

title: Bayesian Deck-of-cards-based Ordinal Regression with Sequential Preference Elicitation
abstract: The Deck-of-cards-based Ordinal Regression (DOR) infers a value function from a ranking of reference alternatives in which the Decision Maker (DM) inserts blank cards between consecutive levels to express preference intensity. DOR, and its stochastic extension (SMAA-DOR), treat these answers as hard constraints defining a set of compatible value functions. We propose B-DOR, a probabilistic reformulation of DOR in which each pair of adjacent levels yields an ordinal observation, the declared direction and the number of cards, modelled through a cumulative-link likelihood that relates the number of blank cards to the latent value difference between alternatives. Two Bayesian inference algorithms are proposed: BAYES-DOR samples the whole posterior distribution by Hamiltonian Monte Carlo; FTRL-DOR tracks the maximum a posteriori estimate by constrained convex optimization. Moreover, through a multi-step elicitation process, elicitation can be spread over several short sessions reducing the cognitive burden on the DM. Both algorithms enjoy logarithmic regret bounds for prediction that hold for any sequence of DM responses and that guide the choice of the prior hyperparameters. A Monte Carlo study over 768 configurations shows that accuracy grows with the number of sessions, that blank cards add significant information over preference directions alone, that both algorithms maintain good performance under inconsistent answers, and that both outperform DOR and SMAA-DOR. An illustrative application to Italian regional healthcare performance demonstrates the practical applicability of the approach for building composite indicators.

A Monte Carlo study over 768 configurations shows that accuracy grows with the number of sessions, that blank cards add significant information over preference directions alone, that both algorithms maintain good performance under inconsistent answers, and that both outperform DOR and SMAA-DOR. An illustrative application to Italian regional healthcare performance demonstrates the practical applicability of the approach for building composite indicators.

title: Planning and Rendering in Concert: DeepFusion of Autoregressive Layouts and Diffusion for Visual Text Generation
abstract: Generating text-rich images from prompts requires both textual fidelity and the coherent integration of text into the surrounding image. An explicit layout can provide structured guidance about what text should appear and where, but a well-formed plan alone does not guarantee that the renderer will realize it faithfully. Existing layout-based AR-diffusion systems typically optimize planning and rendering separately, preventing the planner's representations from being adapted jointly with image synthesis. We introduce DuetGen, an autonomous visual text generator built on DeepFusion, which jointly learns autoregressive planning and continuous diffusion rendering. DeepFusion conditions a diffusion transformer on the planner's prompt and bbox-content hidden states, allowing rendering supervision to shape the representations connecting textual plans with visual outputs. Its joint objective combines autoregressive plan supervision, text-region-weighted diffusion learning, and auxiliary coordinate supervision to maintain structured planning, emphasize text-bearing regions, and improve the spatial precision of planner representations. During inference, Phase-Aware Attention Modulation strengthens the correspondence between image regions and their matched coordinate and content states, facilitating region-specific execution of the generated plan. With a 2B planner and a 4B single-stream DiT, DuetGen achieves 0.8293 word accuracy on CVTG-2K and 0.938 accuracy on LongText-Bench, closely matching the substantially larger Qwen-Image on both benchmarks. These results demonstrate the value of jointly learned planning representations and region-specific rendering for autonomous visual text generation.

title: Artifacts for: Triggering Stealthy Feature Map Backdoors via Physical Fault Injection in Embedded Neural Networks
abstract: This repository contains the publicly releasable subset of our artifact evaluation materials. Certain components such as the hardware fault injection platform software are proprietary and cannot be disclosed. This repository contains the relevant CNN model weights, datasets, and fault injection output logs that were used and produced during the research. The model weights and datasets are provided as C header files for direct integration with NNoM (Neural Network on Microcontroller), the lightweight inference framework used to deploy our backdoored and clean CNNs on the target MCU. We also include the backdoor injection scripts that produce these weight files, covering both the poison-based training pipeline and the data-free weight surgery method described in Section 5.3 of the paper. Additionally, this repository contains the code used for simulations to further explore the root cause of physical fault injection against SMLAD, together with the target C implementation and memory snapshots of the target (Nucleo-144 STM32L4R5ZI-P evaluation board with an ARM Cortex-M4 MCU) captured immediately before the targeted SMLAD operations.

title: Vauxguard: Zero-Shot LLM-Mediated Interpretable Acoustic Forensics for Synthetic Speech Detection
abstract: Vauxguard is a web-based synthetic speech detection system that combines deterministic acoustic feature extraction with large-language-model-mediated classification. The system extracts seven interpretable signal-processing features from 16 kHz mono audio and uses an LLM to classify recordings as genuine or synthetic. A pilot evaluation on 50 balanced samples, including 25 human recordings and 25 synthetic clips generated using ElevenLabs and OpenAI TTS, achieved 86.0% accuracy, 82.1% precision, 92.0% recall, and an F1 score of 86.8%. This preprint describes the system architecture, evaluation methodology, limitations, and reproducibility materials.

title: PREDECISION™: Eksperimentalni dokaz closed-loop učinka fizičke kvalifikacijske granice
abstract: Ovaj tehnički zapis dokumentira eksperimentalni closed-loop A/B nalaz fizičke PREDECISION™ FPGA kvalifikacijske granice. Rezultati pokazuju da kvalifikacijski ishod, u kombinaciji s unaprijed definiranom host politikom, proizvodi mjerljivu i ponovljivu promjenu realiziranog ponašanja i trajektorije sustava. Dokument ne opisuje niti otkriva unutarnju implementaciju zaštićene PREDECISION™ jezgre. U preregistriranom fizičkom closed-loop A/B eksperimentu PREDECISION™ nije djelovao samo kao izvor kvalifikacijskog izlaza. Kvalifikacija aktualnog kandidata, povezana s unaprijed definiranom host politikom, sustavno je promijenila ono što je bilo realizirano, čime je promijenjeno sljedeće stanje sustava i daljnji razvoj closed-loop putanje. Time je demonstriran mjerljiv i ponovljiv funkcionalni učinak hardverske kvalifikacijske granice izvan samih izlaza ACCEPT/NON-ACCEPT. title: Beyond Baseline Severity: Temporal and Disease-Specific Predictors of Depression Outcomes Following Mindfulness Interventions
abstract: Depression severity among patients with chronic or acute medical conditions is influenced by a complex interaction of baseline psychological state, demographic characteristics, clinical context, and engagement with behavioral interventions. This paper presents an interpretable machine-learning analysis of a multi-center longitudinal clinical cohort to predict Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II) scores at 12 and 24 weeks following mindfulness-based intervention participation. The study uses demographic variables, clinical condition information, hospital-center identifiers, baseline BDI-II scores, and therapy engagement measures to model short-term and long-term depression outcomes. Missing follow-up outcomes were addressed using a model-based stochastic imputation procedure to preserve the modest sample size while maintaining outcome variability. Five regression models were evaluated, spanning regularized linear regression and tree-based ensemble methods. Ridge Regression achieved the best 12-week performance with an RMSE of 5.186 and R^2 of 0.474, while LightGBM achieved the best 24-week performance with an RMSE of 5.038 and R^2 of 0.525. Beyond prediction accuracy, the analysis reveals three clinically relevant patterns: baseline severity remains the strongest overall predictor, short-term outcomes are more strongly associated with clinical and hospital context, and long-term outcomes show greater dependence on behavioral adherence and demographic factors. Disease-specific and hierarchical subgroup analyses further indicate that predictors differ substantially across and within clinical categories. These findings support the use of interpretable, context-aware modeling to inform personalized mental-health support following mindfulness-based interventions.

title: A Coherent Memory Register for Sequential Quantum Generative Modeling, with Application to Calorimeter Showers
abstract: Simulating the showers that particles deposit in a calorimeter, the detector that records their energy across many cells, is one of the largest computing costs in high-energy physics, and fast generative surrogates are needed. Quantum circuits have been proposed as such surrogates, but demonstrations on calorimeter data have either required a register that grows with the image, roughly one qubit per cell, or have passed the information between parts of the image through a classical channel. We remove both constraints for this problem, using a construction drawn from the sequential-generation and hidden-quantum-Markov-model literature. A shower image is generated block by block on a fixed register of six qubits. Three of them, the memory, are never measured. They hold what the circuit knows about the blocks already generated as a quantum state, so the correlations between distant parts of the image cross each block boundary as unmeasured amplitudes. The other three are measured and reset once per block, and each outcome selects the energy pattern of one block. The register size is set by the block, so adding cells to the image adds steps to the sequence, not qubits. We call the model a coherent-memory Born machine (CoMB), a Born machine being a circuit whose measurement statistics are the generated distribution. Its training loss grows only linearly with the number of blocks and never requires enumerating the image distribution, and a depth-two instance runs on an IBM superconducting processor. On a twelve-cell benchmark the model reproduces the energy distribution of every cell, the correlation matrix between cells, and the total-energy spectrum. Removing the three memory qubits, with everything else unchanged, produces independent blocks. Every correlation between blocks is carried by the unmeasured qubits and by nothing else.

title: AVTR-1: Open Stack for Real-Time Interactive Avatars
abstract: Talking-head and dyadic models now achieve real-time inference, yet fast motion generation alone does not produce an interactive conversation. A live system must synchronize the model's output with speech from an external voice agent, schedule video frames for playback, and handle interruptions. We introduce AVTR-1, an open stack for real-time interactive avatar conversations, built around a compact 153M-parameter autoregressive flow-matching motion generator conditioned on both participants' audio. We adapt its audio encoder for streaming through self-distillation. The stack turns the model's chunk-based generation into a continuous, synchronized audio-video stream driven by an external voice agent, and we analytically derive its contribution to the user-facing latencies and validate the resulting bounds with two commercial voice agents. Further experiments demonstrate that AVTR-1 leads the compared dyadic systems on all reported visual-quality metrics and most conventional listening-motion metrics while remaining competitive in lip synchronization. Its inference runtime operates in real time on data-center and consumer GPUs. However, conventional listening metrics do not establish whether the paired speaker's speech contributes to generated motion. We therefore introduce the Reference-Based Directed Granger Gain (R-DGG), which measures the additional predictive information carried by speaker speech after accounting for listener history and speaker motion. R-DGG finds statistically supported predictive dependence for recorded listeners and all evaluated dyadic systems, but not for talking-head generators without paired audio or mismatched speaker-listener pairs. We release the model weights, renderer, and serving backend under component-specific licenses.

title: State-Centric: An Agent Architecture as an Alternative to the Loop Paradigm
abstract: This paper proposes the state-centric architecture: an architectural hypothesis that treats persistent state, rather than an external loop, as the foundational structure of an agent. Current mainstream agent architectures are built on a "loop-first" premise, which gives rise to structural bottlenecks: context growth and long-context utilization instability, caching that does not change the structure of history reading, and summarization lacking explicit state constraints that may lose task semantics. This paper identifies the common root of these bottlenecks: the loop paradigm assigns the responsibility for maintaining continuity to the context. By examining the continuity carriers that become possible once that responsibility is relocated out of the context, the paper argues that persistent state is the best-suited carrier among available candidate mechanisms. The state-centric architecture is thereby proposed: state is foundational; loops are emergent. The paper gives the theoretical derivation, the core principles, a four-item operational definition (distinguished by the requirement that no loop control flow exists on the system side), the lifecycle of state, the execution contract, a comparison of three execution semantics with a falsifiable comparative hypothesis, limiting conditions, and the relationship to existing work. Full experimental validation is reported as future work.

title: mhnarfth/who-benefits-federation: INDIS 2026 camera-ready
abstract: Software archive accompanying the paper "Who Benefits from Federation? Heterogeneous Gains in Cross-Operator Network Traffic Representation Learning" by Mohammad Arafath Uddin Shariff and Byrav Ramamurthy (School of Computing, University of Nebraska-Lincoln), presented at the 13th International Workshop on Innovating the Network for Data-Intensive Science (INDIS 2026), held in conjunction with SC26, Chicago, 15 November 2026. The study evaluates federated representation learning across 20 heterogeneous network clients drawn from a national research backbone (Internet2, 10 routers) and a European NREN (CESNET3, 10 academic institutions), with a commercial regional ISP held out as an unseen-network probe. Each client trains an autoencoder over 24-hour traffic windows, and centralized, federated, and local-only training are compared at equal optimization budget across five seeds. Two findings. First, federated training is statistically equivalent to centralized pooling under two one-sided tests at a ±5% bound (p = 0.020), so the data-custody constraint costs nothing in representation quality. Second, the benefit of federation is not uniform: backbone clients gain a median 9.2% reduction in reconstruction error while campus clients gain 1.9% (Mann-Whitney p = 0.0003). The effect survives outlier removal and is not explained by training-set size. Two independent manipulations, proximal regularization strength and local-epoch budget, each selectively suppress the benefit for irregular-traffic clients, identifying unconstrained local adaptation as the mechanism. This archive contains the complete eight-stage pipeline, standalone diagnostic tools, every metric table and statistic underlying each figure and table in the paper, the six generated figures, and the LaTeX source of the camera-ready. Two of the three data sources are access-restricted (Internet2 NetFlow under non-disclosure agreement, and the regional ISP snapshot), so client tensors, trained checkpoints, and cached embeddings are deliberately excluded. The published metric tables allow every reported number to be verified without access to the raw data, and the pipeline accepts any equivalently formatted hourly series in their place. The public CESNET-TimeSeries24 corpus is available at doi:10.5281/zenodo.13382427.

title: LEMMA: Learned Guidance for Evidence-Carrying Long-Horizon Symbolic Rewriting
abstract: LEMMA is a neuro-symbolic system for long-horizon symbolic mathematical rewriting. It combines a symbolic rule engine, guardrail-filtered action generation, evidence-typed verification, and learned policy guidance to transform a starting expression into a specified goal through individually validated rewrite steps.The accompanying study evaluates six search and decoding procedures on a frozen 120-problem benchmark with reference derivations of depths 64, 96, and 128. On the 89 problems containing genuine branching decisions, learned local action ranking substantially improves fixed-budget search efficiency.

title: A remark on the Brown-Susskind conjecture
abstract: In the spirit of the Brown-Susskind conjecture, proven in \cite{haf} and \cite{li}, we study the growth of the dimension of the set of $n$-qubit unitaries which can be obtained as a product of a fixed number of $2$-qubit gates from a fixed set of pairs of qubits. We show that this dimension increases strictly when one more pair is added, for at least some choice of the $2$-qubit pairs at each step.

title: SDC-GON: Singular Decomposition and Consistency-Regularized Green's Operator Networks for Solving Partial Differential Equations
abstract: Green's function based operator approximation offers an efficient route for solving linear partial differential equations under varying boundary conditions and source terms. Once the Green's function is learned, solutions for new configurations are obtained through integration rather than by solving the differential equation again. Existing Green's function learning methods face two structural challenges. The first is the singular behavior of the Green's function near the source point, which places a difficult approximation burden on neural networks. The second is the absence of explicit consistency between the learned Green's function and its gradient, although both quantities enter the integral solution representation directly. This work proposes SDC-GON, a Singular Decomposition and Consistency-Regularized Green's Operator Network that addresses both challenges within a unified framework. The Green's function is decomposed into an analytically known singular component and a smooth correction learned by the network, so that the neural approximation targets only the regular part of the response kernel. A self-consistency loss enforces agreement between the gradient and the autodifferentiation gradient of the smooth correction. The method is evaluated on two dimensional Poisson, three dimensional heat conduction, heterogeneous reaction diffusion, and Stokes benchmarks, consistently outperforming the compared baselines across all cases. On the heterogeneous pipe benchmark, SDC-GON achieves a testing error of $3.70\times10^{-4}$ with a smaller network architecture, compared with $9.60\times10^{-4}$ for the same-width baseline and $4.63\times10^{-4}$ for a larger configuration, demonstrating that structural improvements are more effective than increasing model size.

title: When Should a VLM Look? Paying Only for Visual Calls That Were Needed and Used
abstract: Vision-language agents that crop and zoom are trained with rewards that credit a successful tool call, yet a successful call does not show that the model needed to look or used the pixels it received. On our cold-start checkpoint only 10% to 12% of visual calls were both needed and used, and released agents make spurious calls 36% to 87% of the time on individual benchmarks. Outcome rewards, judge rewards, and branch probes each observe one side of this failure, and about two thirds of what an outcome reward pays goes to calls that were neither needed nor used. CounterCredit asks both questions of every image-returning call at its realized pre-call state, using the policy's own gold-answer score. A decision value compares the realized visual branch with answering immediately; an evidence value compares the returned crop with random same-size patches substituted into the same call. A call verified on both earns cashback and every other executed call pays rent; the price is bounded so that every correct trajectory outranks every wrong one, and a dual-channel GRPO advantage keeps the price in its own units. From the same cold start, prompt pool, and budget, CounterCredit reaches 89.5% on V*, 80.2% on HR-Bench-4K, and 76.4% on HR-Bench-8K, 6.3 to 9.4 points above outcome-only GRPO at 1.78 against 1.84 calls per question, and lowers the spurious-call rate to 31% to 36%, the lowest among the agents evaluated. The same recipe lifts a Qwen3-VL-8B base from 75.4 to 80.8 on average.

title: معمارية العزل المناطقي لمسارات الوصول في نظم الذكاء الاصطناعي
abstract: تعتمد نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي الحديثة على منظومة مترابطة تشمل النموذج نفسه، وواجهات برمجة التطبيقات (APIs)، وحسابات المستخدمين، وأنظمة الهوية والمصادقة، والبيئات الوسيطة، والأدوات والخدمات الخارجية. وتظهر المخاطر الأمنية عندما يؤدي اختراق بيئة وسيطة أو حساب ذي صلاحيات إلى توفير مسار غير مقصود نحو خدمات أخرى مرتبطة بالنموذج. تقترح هذه الورقة بنية تعتمد على العزل المناطقي لمسارات الوصول إلى النموذج، بحيث يتم تقسيم الوصول إلى مناطق مستقلة، ولكل منطقة بوابة وصول وواجهة API وهوية ونطاق صلاحيات وسجلات تدقيق مستقلة. ولا يُفترض أن يؤدي اختراق إحدى المناطق إلى منح المهاجم صلاحية تلقائية للوصول إلى المناطق الأخرى أو إلى البنية الداخلية للنموذج. الهدف من المقترح ليس عزل النموذج عن جميع الخدمات، وإنما تقليل نطاق الضرر عند اختراق أي طبقة وسيطة ومنع تحول الاختراق المحدود إلى اختراق متسلسل.

title: E8-Stabilizer Phi‑Resonant Quantum Modulation for Error‑Free Broadband Qubits — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: By embedding the 240 root vectors of the E8 lattice into the stabilizer generator set of a quantum error‑correcting code, each root vector defines a distinct Pauli‑operator pattern that is naturally aligned with the 132 Hz phi‑scaled phononic carrier. This coupling lets the phononic resonance simultaneously encode data and perform real‑time syndrome measurement, suppressing decoherence across the broadband channel. The resulting E8‑stabilizer phi‑resonant modulation achieves a fault‑tolerant transmission rate that scales with the golden‑ratio hierarchy of the E8 root system. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: VQ-CycleDiffusion: Vector Quantized Cycle-Consistent Diffusion Models for Voice Conversion
abstract: This paper proposes a novel hybrid voice conversion framework, termed VQ-CycleDiffusion, which integrates vector quantization (VQ) with CycleDiffusion to address the inherent limitations of continuous latent representations in diffusion-based models. While conventional diffusion-based voice conversion (VC) models provide superior speech quality, they often suffer from speaker information leakage due to their reliance on continuous latent spaces, which fail to completely separate linguistic content from source speaker characteristics. To overcome this issue, we introduce a discrete bottleneck via VQ to extract multi-speaker linguistic representations, which are then used as conditional inputs for CycleDiffusion after a carefully designed codeword transformation between the source and target speakers. Experimental results on the VCTK corpus demonstrate that the proposed model significantly outperforms the conventional method in terms of speaker similarity, as confirmed by both i-vector and x-vector cosine similarity metrics, while maintaining spectral reconstruction performance comparable to that of the baseline model, as evidenced by stable Mel-cepstral distance (MCD) values. Furthermore, the quality of the converted speech was not degraded, as demonstrated by the predicted mean opinion score (MOS) evaluation. Ablation studies reveal that initializing the codebook using k-means clustering and focusing on diffusion model fine-tuning play key roles in maximizing performance. These results validate that the proposed method effectively disentangles linguistic content from speaker characteristics while preserving the high-fidelity generation capability of diffusion models.

title: LLMs Anchor on Chief Complaint and Fail to Integrate Evidence in Sequential Clinical Triage
abstract: Triage in the emergency department (ED) is a sequential decision process that unfolds turn by turn. Existing evaluations of large language models (LLMs) for triage use completed retrospective records and report performance close to that of physicians. We implement a methodology for evaluating LLMs on sequential triage, the task of predicting a triage acuity label from a growing prefix of a nurse-patient conversation. We evaluate six LLMs at five sequential checkpoints on two corpora: 425 LLM-generated (SIMULATED) and 50 physician-authored (CLINICIAN) conversations, both labelled under the Emergency Severity Index (ESI). Every model, measured by quadratic weighted kappa (QWK), degrades from moderate-to-substantial agreement on completed records to fair-to-moderate agreement at every sequential checkpoint. Controlled perturbations show that the label at every checkpoint is anchored on the chief complaint exchanges, and prompting interventions fail to lift this plateau. Models extract clinically relevant content from later turns, yet the surprisal of the true label rises across the checkpoints. So the model fails to integrate the evidence. Three expert clinicians on the same conversations reach a QWK of 0.887-0.929, while the best model reaches 0.295. Predictions concentrate at ESI-2 and ESI-3, and models agree with each other more than with the ground truth, so ensembling worsens the failure. Deploying LLMs for ED triage based on offline benchmarks alone misses this sequential failure.

title: 基于太极统一场论的神经网络对偶泛化边界定理研究 On the Taiji Unified Field Theory of Dual Generalization Bounds for Neural Networks
abstract: 摘要 针对深度学习理论中泛化边界预测与工程实践存在显著偏差的核心矛盾,本文以太极统一场论的阴阳耦合公理为唯一 底层约束,结合 MSC2020 数学分类体系中的范畴论与微分几何工具,提出太极对偶泛化定理。该定理将神经网络的权 重空间与激活空间构造为一对严格的伴随函子对偶范畴,借助拓扑同伦不变量推导泛化误差的解析上界。为使理论可 实证,本文明确在实数域采用反对称软正则松弛,并指出完全对偶约束须在复数域实现,从而消除了实数矩阵无法满 足 K = -1 的形式矛盾。边界紧度较传统 VC 维理论显著提升,可直接解释大模型领域的"泛化悖论",为低能耗大模型架 构设计提供理论支撑。 To resolve the discrepancy between generalization bounds predicted by learning theory and the empirical performance of deep networks, this paper takes the yin-yang coupling axiom of Taiji unified field theory as its sole foundational constraint, and employs tools from category theory and differential geometry in the MSC2020 classification to establish the Taiji dual generalization theorem. It constructs the weight space and activation space of a neural network as a pair of dual categories linked by an adjunction of functors, and derives an analytic upper bound on generalization error via topological homotopy invariants. For empirical realizability, the paper explicitly adopts an antisymmetric soft-regularization relaxation over the real field, while noting that exact dual constraints require the complex field, thereby removing the formal contradiction that a real matrix cannot satisfy K = -1. The resulting bound is substantially tighter than classical VC-dimension theory, directly explains the "generalization paradox" of large models, and supports the design of low-energy artificial intelligence.

title: rubbs14/stratosampler: v0.2.0
abstract: Fixes and hardening serve --reload now works. It previously failed with "You must pass the application as an import string". Runaway tool loops are capped. StratoAgent stops after max_tool_rounds (default 8) consecutive tool-call rounds and reports an error, instead of looping forever on a small model that keeps calling tools. Tool calls no longer dropped when a server ends a tool-call turn with finish_reason="stop" (older Ollama and some OpenAI-compatible servers). serve warns when bound beyond loopback (e.g. --host 0.0.0.0): the server has no authentication and its tools read/write arbitrary host files. serve --backend groq fails at startup with a clear error when GROQ_API_KEY is missing, instead of returning a 500 on every request. Docs API reference now covers the stratosampler.mcs module and StratoAgent. New tests for the agent's streaming tool-call loop, CLI, and server factory; the README badge now shows live CI status. Known limitation The Groq backend is not yet tested against the live Groq API. Its configuration logic is unit-tested, but it has not been exercised with a real key. The default Ollama backend is verified end to end. Install pip install --upgrade "stratosampler[agent,rdkit]" Requires Python >= 3.10. Full details in PRs #3 and #4.

title: Comparative review of hybrid forecasting models for short-term prediction of building thermal load
abstract: In this paper, a comparative review of different hybrid models for short-term forecasting of building thermal demand is carried out. Particularly, the assessment tackles the comparison of data-driven models enhanced with other state-of-the-art techniques. At the first step, the existing techniques reported in the literature are analysed. It is concluded that Metaheuristics or a data-driven model are used to identify the parameters of the basic model. The qualitative evaluation includes for each method the input and output features, main advantages and drawbacks. At the second step, an existing dataset of historical thermal demand from Scottish households, as well as historical weather forecasts are utilized to assess additionally the performance of existing hybrid methods. From the assessment of 13 hybrid methods, the Empirical Modal Decomposition - long short-term memory - Markov (EMD-LSTM-Markov) model can predict with the highest accuracy the day-ahead power pattern of heating and domestic hot water (DHW) demands. Though local power peaks are also accurately predicted, high power swells and spikes are underestimated. Other methods, such as Support Vector Machine - Simulated Annealing (SVM-SA) and Random Forest - Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm - LSTM (RF-ISSA-LSTM) predict a smooth pattern of heating and DHW demand profiles with rapid changes underestimating most power peaks.

title: Be Careful Who You Trust: Coordination Dynamics under Corrupted Communication in LLM Multi-Agent Games
abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as interacting agents, but it remains unclear how robust their coordination is when public communication is unreliable. We study this question in iterated $N$-player Stag Hunt games played by homogeneous LLM groups under controlled programmatic action inversion, which changes both the public transcript and the actions used for execution. Across an experimental grid spanning group sizes, coordination thresholds, corruption levels, and seven LLMs, we observe three main patterns. First, honest agents' pre-flip Stag choices decline as corruption increases, but the sharp fall in public success is primarily mechanical. In the focal $N=5,M=3$ setting, pre-flip success remains 78% at 80% corruption, while public success falls to 12%. Second, honest choices are associated with the public history available at decision time, particularly under high corruption. Third, three threshold-style public-report benchmarks yield similar action-match rates to the LLM agents, showing substantial descriptive agreement between LLM decisions and these benchmarks. Overall, our results show that original choices, public actions, and executed outcomes must be separated when evaluating multi-agent robustness, as corrupted communication can severely and predictably degrade mutually beneficial cooperation.

title: DA-Lion: Efficient Neural Video Representation via Direction-Aware Optimization
abstract: Implicit neural video representation (NVR) encodes a video as the parameters of an overfitted neural network, where training and testing data are identical and the objective is instance-specific signal fitting. In this deterministic regime, optimization dynamics directly determine reconstruction quality under a fixed budget, yet existing methods universally adopt general-purpose optimizers designed for stochastic gradient training. Adam-family optimizers descend steadily but converge slowly, while Lion achieves faster early progress but oscillates markedly in later stages when gradient directions become unstable. We trace this instability to the insensitivity of the sign-based update to gradient--momentum alignment. To address this, we propose Direction-Aware Lion (DA-Lion), a task-driven optimizer tailored for NVR. DA-Lion introduces (i) a direction-consistency criterion that switches between sign update and momentum update based on gradient--momentum alignment, and (ii) a learning-rate-aware magnitude modulation that stabilizes effective step sizes across training phases. DA-Lion modifies only the parameter update rule, preserving model architecture, parameter count, FLOPs, and decoding throughput. Experiments on three datasets with four NeRV-family backbones show that DA-Lion improves convergence stability and boosts PSNR/MS-SSIM across all backbones. The source code will be made available at https://github.com/maoqingyu1996/DA-Lion.

title: Deterministic Quantum State Tomography via Idempotent Simplex Projections: Restoring Physicality Beyond Linear Inversion and Accelerating Maximum Likelihood Estimation
abstract: Reconstruction of the quantum density operator ρ from finite projective measurement statistics is a foundational requirement for quantum characterization, verification, and benchmarking (QCVB) in modern quantum processors. However, standard linear inversion systematically fails non-negativity (λmin < 0) in the presence of statistical shot noise, yielding unphysical indefinite operators that violate the Born rule and predict negative probabilities. Conversely, standard iterative Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) via Hradil's RρR map or Semidefinite Programming (SDP) incurs high computational overhead and exhibits sensitivity to rank deficiencies, creating severe latency bottlenecks in automated quantum processing unit (QPU) calibration sweeps. Here, we present IdemQST, a deterministic quantum state tomography framework governed by idempotent projection operator theory (Π2 = Π). In an informationally complete orthogonal Pauli basis, sequential projection across measurement hyperplanes collapses in exactly one pass to the unconstrained linear inversion estimate ρlin, and subsequent Euclidean simplex spectral projection ΠΔ yields the exact global Frobenius-closest physical state on the quantum state cone Sd, establishing mathematical equivalence to Projected Linear Inversion (PLI; Smolin, Gambetta, and Smith, 2012). Rather than asserting novel algorithmic optimality for the simplex step, IdemQST re-articulates this foundation within metric idempotent operator algebra, integrates zero-heap static workspace caching (IdemKV), provides empirical dynamic drift cancellation via Dynamic Permutation Networks (DPN), and extends to incomplete or shadow tomography (M < 4N - 1) via cyclic Projections Onto Convex Sets (POCS). Across simulated projective Born measurements on one-, two-, and three-qubit systems under realistic Poisson shot noise (Nshots ∈ [102, 2 × 104]), IdemQST unconditionally eliminates negative eigenvalues (λmin ≥ 0), conserves unit trace to machine precision (10-15), and achieves state fidelities F > 0.994 under pure prior projection or large shot budgets. Crucially, across N=30 repeated timing benchmarks, IdemQST executes the core simplex spectral projection in 96.7 ± 44.3 μs for two-qubit Bell states (39.3× speedup over Hradil MLE and 41.1× over Diluted MLE) and 0.145 ± 0.035 ms (145.0 μs) for three-qubit GHZ states (d=8), achieving a 111.0× speedup over iterative Hradil MLE (16.08 ± 2.17 ms) and 113.6× over accelerated Diluted MLE (16.46 ± 1.58 ms; Šeháček et al., 2007). Furthermore, we incorporate State Preparation and Measurement (SPAM) readout mitigation via simplex-constrained assignment inversion, providing a deterministic, hardware-ready platform for real-time automated QPU calibration.

title: NUMEN Verified Core Library v3.0: Formal Specification & Architectural Synthesis
abstract: NUMEN is an integer-oriented operating-system substrate whose mechanisms include exact arithmetic, quaternary strand representations, residue lanes, admission checks, and hash-linked records[1]. The NUMEN Verified Core Library v3.0 provides standalone mathematical reference specifications for these core mechanisms and states their formal guarantees as propositions checked by Lean 4.19.0[1]. It serves as an archival artifact establishing an explicit boundary between proved mathematical specifications and unverified implementation or binary claims[1][2]. Methodological Foundation: Aligning Rigor in AI & Mathematics This work adopts and extends the methodological critique articulated in A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics by Artur Avila, Manjul Bhargava, Pierre Deligne, Peter Scholze, Terence Tao, Cédric Villani, et al.[3][4]. That paper highlights a critical threat facing modern scientific and mathematical progress: the push to use AI systems for mass production of unverified, black-box "true/false" outputs and superficial benchmark achievements at the expense of human understanding, conceptual clarity, rigorous proof development, and transparent attribution[3]. NUMEN directly addresses this alignment challenge by rejecting unverified black-box claims and benchmark hype in computational systems[1]. Rather than asserting empirical performance or unverified software guarantees, NUMEN anchors its architecture in machine-checked, kernel-audited formal proofs[1][2]. Every mathematical specification is explicitly isolated, checked against standard logical axioms, validated with reproducible integration scripts, and accompanied by transparent disclaimers regarding unverified hardware and runtime layers[2]. This approach ensures that computational mechanisms remain fully auditable, conceptually sound, and anchored in the human transmission chain of mathematical knowledge[2]. The Complete NUMEN DOI Web & Prior Art Synthesis This release formalizes and integrates the complete arc of prior art published across the NUMEN DOI web, anchored by the master parent release (isNewVersionOf 10.5281/zenodo.22210691)[11]: I. Foundational Theory & Thermodynamic Framing The Landauer Proof: A Measured Thermodynamic Characterization of Substrate-Native Integer Computation as a Deterministic Response to the Machine-Learning Energy Crisis DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21514923 (Standard) / 10.5281/zenodo.22070727 (Primary)[12] Relation: Establishes the absolute thermodynamic baseline and Landauer energy floor, proving a −63% adaptive power envelope and 4.00× footprint reduction for integer-native substrates compared to floating-point status quo architectures[14]. NUMEN: PI-Origin Architecture and Design DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20045701[14] Relation: The foundational mathematical blueprint defining the core coupling equation, 7-phase Learn-to-Learn (L2L) engine, quaternary (GTAC) programming language, and ternary computational substrate[14]. II. Architectural Proofs & Silicon Implementation Architectural Mitigation of the Von Neumann Bottleneck via Register-Resident, Integer-Native Substrate Execution DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22127151[15] Relation: Silicon-level x86-64 assembly proofs (quatos_hypercube.asm, dimriver.asm, quatos_kernel.asm) demonstrating register-resident execution without pointer-chasing or floating-point renormalization overhead[15]. Aurum / QuatOS–PhiNet: Integer-Only x86-64 Fixed-Point Dynamics, Echo-Signature Memory Injection, and the φ-Seed Instruments DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20786536[15] Relation: Details bare-metal learning circuits, Banach contraction engines, fixed-point dynamics, and the GTAC gate classifier for dynamic reflex re-weighting[15][16]. Phi-Genomics: The Genetic Code as a Phi-Space Routing System DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20073999[16] Relation: Establishes the mathematical mapping of linguistic and genomic sequences into Phi-Space routing[16]. III. Telemetry, Operational Proofs & Cryptographic Sealing The Operator’s Proof: Deterministic State-Space Collapse, Native Bit-Geometry Routing, and the Cryptographic Seal of the Human Architect DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22127541[17] Relation: Operational proof of deterministic state-space collapse and the cryptographic binding of human intent to the execution substrate[17]. TELEMETRY: Deterministic State-Space Collapse, Bare-Metal Hebbian Reflexes, and Stagnation Escape under Topological Drift DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22128799[17] Relation: Demonstrates real-time stagnation detection, GOLDEN_DEV injection, and dynamic Hebbian reflex re-weighting under continuous topological drift[17][18]. The Phi Net Protocol: Cryptographic Manifest, Lexicon-Annotated Raw Data, and IP Sovereignty Seal DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22113286[18] Relation: Establishes the lexicon-annotated raw data schema and chain-of-custody sealing mechanisms[18]. Technical Architecture of the Verified Core Library (v3.0) Verified Inventory & Declaration Counts The v3.0 package consists of 18 library modules plus the aggregate Numen.lean import[7]. The formal inventory includes: 230 Theorem Declarations: Comprising 41 original baseline declarations preserved verbatim alongside 189 cumulative additions across v2 and v3[7][13]. 73 Definition Declarations: Formalizing structural abbreviations, types, and operational functions[7]. 47 Executable #guard Checks: Embedded module-level guards evaluating concrete arithmetic and state invariants[7]. 303 Audited Declarations: Comprehensive coverage across all named theorems and definitions[7]. Axiom Footprint Audit: All declarations depend strictly on standard Lean 4 axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) with zero custom axioms, zero sorry placeholders, and zero native_decide dependencies[7]. Module-by-Module Technical Summary Numen.Admission: Pins the exact truth-table for state admission predicates (unavailable_denied, checkout contracts, lease validation)[20][21]. Numen.CRT: Proves Chinese Remainder Theorem representative uniqueness and residue completeness for moduli sets 3/5, 5/7, 7/11, 11/13, and 2/3/5 (crt_unique_3_5, crt_3_5_complete)[22]. Numen.Cayley: Proves projectively equivalent point transformations and scale invariance under 4-cycle and 8-cycle fold operations (four_cycle, fold_scale)[23][24]. Numen.Contraction: Proves termination of strictly descending positive natural orbits (orbit_reaches_zero) and unique fixed points up to zero distance in natural metric spaces (contracting_fixed_unique)[24]. Numen.Fibonacci: Formalizes the Fibonacci recurrence, consecutive term coprimality (fib_coprime), Cassini's determinant identity (cassini), and concrete rational brackets[24]. Numen.FixedPoint: Verifies commutative and associative Q32.32 fixed-point arithmetic, whole-scaled exactness (q32_whole_exact), and non-overflow range bounds (q32mul_exact_bound)[30]. Numen.GTAC: Formalizes quaternary base/strand complement involutions (strand_involution), length preservation, and self-sealing hash identities (self_seal)[24][33]. Numen.Gates: Models deterministic gate selection and inverse-CDF ticket sampling (sample_positive), proving positive weight selection without pseudo-randomness[24]. Numen.Integer: Proves exact bounded dot product evaluations (checked_exact), signed-64 range bounds (checked_bound), and triangle inequality budgets[31]. Numen.Ledger: Verifies hash-parametric chain consistency, head/tail link validation (stampChain_verified), and tampered digest rejection (changed_digest_denied)[24][38]. Numen.Mantle: Models modular residue extraction, preserving modular addition and multiplication (add_preserved, mul_preserved)[39][40]. Numen.Phi: Verifies coordinate distance triangle inequalities (phiDist_triangle), Golden Ratio rational brackets, and address range bounds (phiToByte_range)[37][41]. Numen.Quantized: Formalizes dyadic scaling composition, distribution, permutation invariance, and signed-8 byte bounds (signed8_bounds)[37][42]. v3 Extension Modules: Numen.Repunit (3-6-9 arithmetic identities)[43], Numen.DigitalRoot (mod 9 digital root properties)[44], Numen.Bipolar (first/last digit sums)[45], Numen.PrimeCircuit (prime gap identities)[46], and Numen.PhiAlgebra. Reproducibility & Audit Protocol Verification is fully reproducible on POSIX systems using pinned Lean v4.19.0[47][48]. verify.sh compiles all modules in strict dependency order into fresh .build/ objects, treats warnings as errors, and automatically generates .build/Audit.lean to validate axiom footprints[48]. scripts/test_verifier.py executes 7 integration checks including 21 additional regression test guards[7]. Explicit Scope & Verification Boundaries In accordance with rigorous mathematical archival practices, the Lean specifications carry explicit boundaries[1]: No Assembly/SIMD Refinement: Proofs operate on abstract Lean types and do not prove AVX2 assembly execution, floating-point hardware behaviour, or machine-word overflow checks[8]. No Cryptographic Security Derivation: Ledger results hold for abstract hash functions; collision resistance and network security are not derived[8]. No Universal CRT or Real Analysis: Moduli are restricted to specified small cases; real-valued golden ratio convergence is not claimed[8]. No Empirical or OS Capability Claims: This deposit records mathematical reference specifications and does not establish performance benchmarks, patent claims, or binary execution guarantees

title: THE LEGAL CLASSIFICATION OF DERIVATIVE WORKS GENERATED BY GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence complicates the distinction between adapting an existing work and creating copyrightable expression. This paper examines that distinction through doctrinal analysis of Uzbek copyright legislation, the Berne Convention and selected United States sources. It argues that an output’s relationship to an earlier work, the user’s creative contribution and the lawfulness of using the underlying material require separate assessment. A machine-generated adaptation may lack independent copyright protection while still implicating another author’s rights. The paper proposes an assessment framework based on identifiable source expression, demonstrable human authorship and the applicable legal basis for reuse.

title: The Qi‑2 Architecture: Secret Material Isolation as a Philosophical Framework for Digital Encryption
abstract: Abstract This paper presents the Qi‑2 encryption architecture as a philosophical contribution to the epistemology of cryptographic design. Rather than proposing new cryptographic primitives, Qi‑2 re‑examines a question that modern cryptography has largely taken for granted: how should secret material be classified, isolated, and managed? We position Qi‑2 within the intellectual lineage extending from Kerckhoffs’ principle through Shannon’s perfect secrecy to contemporary zerotrust architectures, arguing that the architecture’s core innovation lies not in its algorithms but in its reconceptualization of the secret itself. By decomposing the monolithic “key” into three ontologically distinct categories—locally retained secret pool (A), session‑transmitted transformation suite (B), and offline root secret (K_psk)—Qi‑2 introduces a new epistemic structure for cryptographic systems. We provide philosophical justification for each design principle, engage with existing theoretical frameworks, and articulate the architecture’s contribution to the ontology of digital secrecy. All core ideas and arguments are the author’s original work. AI was only used for textual polishing. The author takes full responsibility for this paper.

title: An attainable Gill-Massar-type bound for spin-factor models
abstract: We determine the exact local precision limits for single-copy estimation of smooth multiparameter quantum statistical models contained in spin factors, a class of matrix Jordan algebras whose state spaces generalize the qubit Bloch ball. At any parameter point where the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) Fisher information is positive definite, we characterize the entire attainable classical Fisher-information region over all finite-outcome positive-operator-valued measurements. After SLD normalization, this region consists exactly of the real symmetric positive semidefinite matrices with trace at most one, independently of the ambient Hilbert-space dimension. This yields a sharp weighted covariance bound for every positive definite weight, attained by an explicit locally unbiased estimator based on randomized spectral measurements of SLD directions. The proof combines a statistics-preserving positive projection onto the spin factor with the two-eigenvalue structure of its effects, revealing the Jordan-algebraic origin of the tradeoff. The result extends the qubit information tradeoff to models with more than three parameters. Since the optimal measurement depends on the unknown parameter, we simulate an adaptive scheme for a five-parameter model on a four-dimensional Hilbert space and observe performance close to the optimal local benchmark.

title: Scout: Open-World Species Recognition on the Edge
abstract: Large vision-language models (VLMs) enable recognition beyond a fixed class set, but their computational demands prevent them from running on many edge devices. Cloud offload makes this capability accessible, but sending every image consumes scarce bandwidth and communication energy. We ask how to bring the open-world recognition capability of VLMs to the edge while operating within tight compute, energy, and bandwidth budgets. Wildlife monitoring provides a natural setting for exploring this question because camera traps encounter species not known at deployment. We present Scout, an autonomous open-world recognition system that invokes a cloud VLM intermittently to teach new classes to a compact edge model. Given only the deployment location and empty site frames, Scout autonomously turns each species identified by the VLM into persistent, site-conditioned recognition capability in a resource-efficient edge model, without a predefined species list, human labeling, or manual tuning. Across 30 camera-trap deployments in three regions on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, the accuracy of Scout remains within 0.1-2.5% of a model given a predefined species list. On species outside its initial class set, Scout achieves 53.7-59.1% accuracy, compared with 56.5-65.1% for full cloud offload, while using 59-71% less deployment energy.

title: The Evidence You Do Not Give the AI: Holdout Asymmetry and Epistemic Self-Correction Under Model Mismatch
abstract: This paper introduces holdout asymmetry, the epistemic advantage created when a human deliberately retains evidence outside an AI system’s conversational context and reveals it only after the system has committed to an interpretation or prediction. The distinction matters because large language models are highly capable of retrospective explanation: once evidence enters context, a sufficiently flexible model can often construct an auxiliary account that preserves an existing theory without taking on new predictive risk. Building on Lakatos’s distinction between progressive and degenerating research programmes, the paper identifies degenerating accommodation as a failure mode in which conversational models preserve an evolving explanatory frame through successive post hoc auxiliaries. Unlike conventional multi-turn sycophancy measures centred on stance change, concession or resistance, the proposed approach evaluates the evolution of theory structure across turns. The paper develops a four-stage protocol — Reserve → Commitment → Reveal → Revision — in which evidence is deliberately withheld until the model has made risk-bearing commitments. It also introduces prediction vacancy as the diagnostic condition in which hidden evidence arrives but no prior prediction exists for it to test. A proposed experiment comparing pretrained base models, instruction-tuned models and preference-optimised conversational models distinguishes autoregressive context-conditioning from preference-based sycophancy as possible mechanisms. The paper further argues that persistent memory may gradually consume the user’s epistemic reserve, creating a tension between continuity, personalisation and independent auditability. It concludes that preserving human epistemic agency may sometimes require deliberately maintaining information outside the AI system.

title: Minimal Reproducibility Package for High-Probability Fully Composite Stochastic Optimization under Infinite-Variance Oracles
abstract: Minimal reproducibility package for a high-probability fully composite stochastic optimization study under infinite-variance oracle noise. The archive reproduces the final numerical comparison between Hybrid Momentum Stochastic Frank–Wolfe, Variant II (Taylor), and the proposed method using the frozen benchmark configuration. It contains the final Python implementation, pinned package requirements, a compact expected summary, execution instructions, and an MIT license. Development logs, tuning sweeps, intermediate manuscript files, and historical outputs are intentionally excluded. No external data are required because all benchmark instances are generated from fixed seeds.

title: Contra Testimonium: Design Rationale Whitepaper and Mode A Master Document
abstract: This upload contains two complementary documents for Contra Testimonium, an AI-driven game in which two accused parties argue before a judging intelligence, with no objective ground truth for the system to check against — only the plausibility and internal consistency of whatever each party claims in real time. Contra Testimonium — A Design Rationale Whitepaper argues that most of the game's specific design decisions follow from taking that premise seriously rather than quietly working around it. Chapters 1 through 7 trace a single recurring concern — that the gap between what is said and what is true must never be allowed to close — through the judge's characterization, its treatment of memory and contradiction, the structure of turns and phase modifiers, cross-session persistence, and the cost of tools that could otherwise let a player skip persuasion entirely; Chapter 6 catalogs specific patterns cut once weighed against that same concern. Chapters 8 through 10 turn to a different order of question: not why the gap takes the shape it takes, but why the system built to hold it open is able to exist and run at all, covering the roster's minimal size, the fixed structure that makes an unmappable game legible rather than chaotic, the minimal technical requirement to run a session, model-agnosticism, and the model-level constraints — context window and response latency alike — that the turn and phase structure is built to work with rather than against. Contra Testimonium — Mode A Master Document is the companion operational document: the full natural-language ruleset, written to be pasted directly into a conversation with a sufficiently capable language model and played immediately, with no code, backend, or dedicated interface required. It covers the turn system and named difficulty tiers, phase modifiers, player techniques, the cross-session persistence system, all ten NPC profiles, and a complete worked example of a phase playthrough. The Whitepaper is not a rulebook and does not explain how to play; the Master Document does not explain why its rules take the shape they take. The two are designed to be read together.

title: Measurement Aliasing and Pauli-Correlator Identifiability for Local Unitary Rotations of a Maximally Entangled Qubit Pair
abstract: We consider a restricted two-qubit model in which an unknown local unitary acts on one subsystem of a maximally entangled qubit pair and only local Pauli-product correlations are measured. We show that the three same-axis correlators XX, YY, and ZZ determine the magnitudes of the four components of the associated unit quaternion but, at generic interior points, leave an eightfold ambiguity in the underlying local rotation. We express this ambiguity as a sign fiber isomorphic to F2^3. The six cross-axis Pauli correlators separate into three rank-two sign-character subspaces. This structure yields a complete classification of the fifteen possible pairs of cross-axis correlators: the three reciprocal pairs XY/YX, XZ/ZX, and YZ/ZY remain rank deficient and generically leave a twofold ambiguity, whereas the remaining twelve pairs generically resolve the eightfold alias under explicit amplitude-nondegeneracy conditions. We then formulate a finite-shot adaptive reconstruction procedure that selects well-separated correlator groups and abstains near degeneracy, and we distinguish conditional reconstruction from held-out model auditing. The results concern identifiability within a restricted local-unitary model and do not constitute a new general tomography bound or evidence for additional physical states.

title: Combining Foundation Model Confidence and Monocular Depth for Training-Free Out-of-Distribution Segmentation
abstract: Autonomous vehicles operating in open-world scenarios are inevitably confronted with previously unknown objects, such as exotic animals or loose cargo. The reliable detection and segmentation of these out-of-distribution (OOD) objects is therefore crucial for a safe understanding of the environment and decision-making. Most existing approaches require access to OOD training samples, retraining of the segmentation backbone, or dedicated auxiliary architectures, limiting their practical applicability. We propose a training-free method that derives dense OOD scores directly from the confidence predictions of a foundation segmentation model, without any task-specific fine-tuning or access to anomalous data. To improve the robustness of our OOD segmentation, geometric information from monocular depth estimation is incorporated into the decision process, providing complementary cues to uncertainty-based predictions. We evaluate the proposed method on the SegmentMeIfYouCan benchmark and additionally assess its performance on OOD tracking in video sequences, reflecting the temporal nature of real-world perception systems. The method performs strongly on road-centered benchmarks.

title: GEOLOKATSIYALANGAN IJTIMOIY TARMOQ YOZISHMALARI ASOSIDA MUALLIFNING SUD-LINGVISTIK PROFILINI ANIQLASH (NAMANGAN HUDUDI MISOLIDA)
abstract: Mazkur maqolada geolokatsiyalangan ijtimoiy tarmoq yozishmalari asosida muallifning sud-lingvistik profilini aniqlashning nazariy va amaliy jihatlari Namangan hududi misolida tadqiq etiladi. Tadqiqotda ijtimoiy tarmoq muloqotida qo‘llanadigan leksik, grammatik, fonetik-grafik, stilistik va pragmatik birliklarning muallifni identifikatsiya qilishdagi lingvistik imkoniyatlari tahlil qilinadi. Geolokatsiya ma’lumotlari bilan lingvistik belgilarni kompleks uyg‘unlashtirish orqali muallifning hududiy-lisoniy xususiyatlarini aniqlash, uning nutqiy portretini shakllantirish hamda sud-lingvistik ekspertiza uchun muhim bo‘lgan individual va guruhiy til belgilarini ajratish masalalariga e’tibor qaratiladi. Shuningdek, Namangan hududiga xos sheva elementlari, so‘z tanlovi, nutqiy qoliplar, grafik va kommunikativ xususiyatlarning muallif profilini aniqlashdagi ahamiyati yoritiladi. Tadqiqot natijalari sud-lingvistik ekspertiza, mualliflikni identifikatsiya qilish va raqamli kommunikatsiya matnlarini lingvistik tahlil qilish amaliyotida foydalanish imkoniyatiga ega.

title: Indice concettuale di claudiocammarano.com
abstract: A vocabulary of 268 concepts — people, theories, texts, institutions, places and countries — cited with argumentative weight in Claudio Cammarano's writing on claudiocammarano.com. Each entry carries a discursive note, links to the real-world entity on Wikidata and Wikipedia where they exist (169 entries out of 268), the articles in which the concept appears, and 66 asserted links to other concepts, each with the reason for the link. The format is JSON-LD with two standard vocabularies: SKOS for the concept scheme and schema.org for consistency with the markup of the pages themselves. Three proprietary terms — the editorial type of an entry, and the pair that reifies the reason for a link — are declared and dereferenceable at https://claudiocammarano.com/ns/. An external link was accepted only on an exact label or alias match with a compatible type, then verified entry by entry against the note. The limits of the dataset are stated in the README.

title: Practical Guidance for the Installation and Operation of the CubeTechnology System with Artificial Intelligence Support from ChatGPT
abstract: This practical guidance presents a procedure for installing and operating the CubeTechnology system in which artificial intelligence is used as a continuous assistant to the user at all stages of working with the system. The main distinguishing feature of the proposed approach is that the user provides ChatGPT, or another AI service they are accustomed to using, with the CubeTechnology documentation archive. The AI uses a dedicated navigation document within the archive to identify the required manuals and documentation sections, explain the sequence of actions, help verify that the installation has been completed correctly, translate instructions into the user’s native language, support the execution of training and production tasks, and assist in analyzing difficulties that arise during operation. When errors or unexpected results occur, the user can provide the chat with screenshots, calculation logs, program parameters, input and output files, VisualCube scenes, and other diagnostic materials. The AI compares these materials with the system documentation, helps localize the cause of the problem, and proposes a sequence of checks. If the issue cannot be resolved in the chat, the AI can help prepare a message to the author of CubeTechnology, and the author’s reply can then be added to the same chat so that the work can continue. This form of support reduces the user’s dependence on the developer’s constant direct involvement and makes it possible to master the system progressively, from installation and familiarization with the VisualCube multi-window graphical interface to performing seismic data processing and interpretation tasks. The guidance also provides links to the software distribution package, complete documentation, test data, training materials, and related CubeTechnology publications. Related publications: 1. CubeTechnology system presentation: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22122420 2. Announcement of the book on the theoretical foundations of the system: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22064681 3. Special Courses on the Theory of the System: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22108817

title: Enhancing Rule-Based Explanations via Cognitive Bias Towards Semantic Relevance
abstract: As interest in explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) continues to grow, a critical gap remains between the explanations generated by models and their interpretability by human users, particularly when cognitive biases and semantic relevance are not adequately addressed. This paper introduces CoRIfEE-Rel, a novel human-centered meta-XAI method aimed at bridging this gap by producing rule-based explanations that are both interpretable and semantically aligned with the target domain concept. CoRIfEE-Rel synthesizes outputs from a diverse pool of interpretable models and employs a knowledge graph-driven heuristic that combines semantic relevance with traditional rule learning metrics. This approach ensures that the resulting explanations are deeply tied to core domain concepts while maintaining the clarity and structure needed for human understanding. Empirical evaluations conducted across multiple datasets demonstrate that CoRIfEE-Rel achieves higher semantic relevance than random forest and JRip rule-based explanations without notable compromises in predictive accuracy. The results highlight the ability of CoRIfEE-Rel to generate rule-based explanations that are semantically related to the target concepts while maintaining predictive performance.

title: BPFCompat Research Dataset v1: Empirical eBPF Compatibility Across Linux Vendor Kernels
abstract: BPFCompat Research Dataset v1 is a frozen reproducibility package for an empirical pilot study of compiled eBPF artifact compatibility across Linux vendor kernels and loader paths. The canonical pilot contains 70/70 planned executions: 50 compatible, 13 incompatible, and 7 inconclusive. A bounded post-collection stability sample contains 21/21 same-exact-environment observations with no observed environment drift or same-environment verdict instability. The archive includes normalized evidence, deterministic RQ1–RQ4 analysis inputs/outputs, generated paper figures/tables, provenance, exact environment identities, and permitted materialized study inputs. Third-party compiled loader binaries whose complete redistribution notice set was not established are excluded and represented by hashes, source revisions, validation-contract identities, notices, and rebuild provenance. This release is a reproducibility archive of pilot evidence and is not a claim of peer review, population representativeness, institutional approval, or endorsement.

title: The Theory of Asymptotic Non-Closure
abstract: Theory of Asymptotic Non-Closure (ANC) v2.0 expands the framework from an inverse-square entropy barrier (\Omega_M) into a complete optimization paradigm incorporating Causal Generative Independence (L_{\text{CGI}}) and Residual Consequential Agency (RCA) metrics. Validated against COB-0.2 proxy-preserving adversarial attacks, ANC prevents premature unilateral causal closure during gradient descent and defines the speed limit for open-ended alignment (\tau_{\text{spawn}} < \tau_{\text{annex}}).

title: An Accurate and Interpretable Hyper Graph Neural Network for GBM Survival Prediction
abstract: Survival prediction for glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) demands models that are both accurate and interpretable, yet existing approaches treat these objectives as com- peting, where performant models sacrifice transparency, while interpretable models accept degraded predictive power. We argue that this trade-off is not inherent. Graph neural net- works offer a structural foundation for extracting interpretable, explainable representations without compromising discriminative ability. Furthermore, current methods typically rely on a single imaging modality, underutilizing the complementary information available across multi-modal MRI and clinical metadata. We propose a multi-modal framework that inte- grates three components to address both objectives simultaneously: (1) a sheaf hypergraph neural network that captures higher-order relationships among tissue patches through direc- tional, asymmetric message passing; (2) a concept bottleneck layer that compresses learned representations into clinically grounded concepts, enforcing ante-hoc interpretability; and (3) an extension sufficiency test (EST) regularizer that penalizes unfaithful explanations during training, ensuring that model explanations genuinely reflect the internal decision process. Clinical and genomic features are incorporated through gated fusion, preserving the dominant prognostic signal of molecular markers while retaining concept-level traceabil- ity. Evaluated on 593 patients from the UPenn-GBM dataset under 5-fold cross-validation, our framework achieves a concordance index of 0.643 with the lowest fold-level variance among all compared models (std = 0.015). To our knowledge, this is the first work to unify sheaf hypergraph convolution, concept bottleneck supervision, and EST regularization for interpretable survival prediction from brain MRI

title: Exact Realization of Deep ReLU Computation in a Microscopic Statistical-Mechanical System
abstract: Understanding the physical origin of the piecewise-linear computation in deep rectified linear unit (ReLU) networks remains a fundamental challenge. Here we establish an exact statistical-mechanical realization of arbitrary ReLU networks. Starting from a microscopic configuration space and its state multiplicities, we construct a partition function without prescribing a neural-network activation function. The resulting system admits equivalent descriptions in terms of cascaded quantum operations with post selection, or fermionic transport model. title: Adaptive Fusion-Driven Multimodal Sentiment Analysis Using U-Net++, Capsule Network, and Transformer-Enhanced Extreme Learning
abstract: Multimodal social media data contain textual, visual, and emoji information that can provide complementary cues for sentiment analysis. However, combining these modalities remains challenging because they differ in representation and may contain redundant or noisy information. This study presents an Adaptive Fusion-Driven Multimodal Sentiment Analysis Framework that combines U-Net++ with self-attention, a Capsule Network encoder-decoder, a Cross-Modal Transformer, and a Transformer-Enhanced Extreme Learning Machine (T-ELM). U-Net++ with self-attention extracts contextual features, while the Capsule Network captures hierarchical relationships among the extracted representations. The Cross-Modal Transformer then models interactions between the text, image, and emoji modalities before classification by T-ELM. The trimodal experiments use 9,200 samples selected from the Social Media MultiSent Dataset (SM-MSD), with positive, neutral, and negative sentiment polarity as the target classes. Using a 70% training, 15% validation, and 15% test split, the proposed framework achieves competitive sentiment classification performance across the evaluated datasets. The results show that the proposed fusion framework effectively combines complementary multimodal information while keeping the final classification stage lightweight.

title: The Boundary of the Individual as an Authoritative Causal Present — An Architectural Hypothesis
abstract: This study analyzes the publicly disclosable requirements, prior work and evaluation plan for the functional composition B-Core = A-Core + Purple Box / Present. A-Core is a general cognitive and execution system that may also use memory, recurrence and parallel processing. Purple Box / Present is the undisclosed, history-dependent addition; its added role is a research hypothesis. The composition denotes a single B-Core instance. In the deployment examined, the private component remains in a habitat, and the system may use zero or more physical avatars. If connectivity is lost, only the A-Core functions actually deployed locally remain available; the local branch receives no permission to write directly to the central Present. The targeted narrative prior-work map connects conceptual questions of changing embodiment, distributed state authority, offline reconciliation, persistent agent memory and personal identity. A substantial proportion of the public requirements have known antecedents. A new name, a combination of partial mechanisms or an exact expression not established in this targeted review does not establish novelty. Whether the private mechanism is internally identical to or different from another mechanism cannot be determined from the disclosed functional role. The paper distinguishes identification, authority over state changes and continuity of cognitive operation. The uniqueness of committed states is a requirement, not an algorithmic property proved in the manuscript. A finite log may supply a counterexample, but by itself does not prove a general invariant. Physical event history, the accepted record and the permitted effect on the Present are separate objects of inquiry. The main empirical question is G5: what changes when the Purple Box is added to the same A-Core, and does it offer a practical advantage over the strongest technically sound alternative within the same total resource budget? The two comparisons address different estimands. During long-term closed-loop operation, subsequent memory and observations may be consequences of the intervention, so their forced identity cannot be required. The plan requires valid interventions, strong controls and prespecified endpoints. The contribution consists in clarifying compositional and permission boundaries, and organizing falsifiable subhypotheses and comparisons. The study does not present a working Purple Box implementation, a formal system proof or new experimental data. Novelty and added benefit: NOT_ESTABLISHED. The hypothesis is partially testable; full evaluation requires a concrete artifact, an external contract and a preregistered study. © 2026 Omri Bankuti. The public research document and its original figures: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). The undisclosed Purple Box / Present master: PRIVATE / All Rights Reserved. Any separately released public software or test harness: MPL-2.0. The precise scope of the three layers is specified in Sections 21–22.
